Presidential Documents
46055
Federal Register
Vol. 69, No. 146
Friday, July 30, 2004
Title 3—
The President
Executive Order 13350 of July 29, 2004
Termination of Emergency Declared in Executive Order
12722 With Respect to Iraq and Modification of Executive
Order 13290, Executive Order 13303, and Executive Order
13315
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws
of the United States of America, including the International Emergency
Economic Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq .)(IEEPA), the National Emer-
gencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1601 et seq .)(NEA), section 5 of the United Nations
Participation Act, as amended (22 U.S.C. 287c)(UNPA), and section 301
of title 3, United States Code,
I, GEORGE W. BUSH, President of the United States of America, have
determined that the situation that gave rise to the declaration of a national
emergency with respect to Iraq in Executive Order 12722 of August 2,
1990, has been significantly altered by the removal of the regime of Saddam
Hussein and other developments. I hereby terminate the national emergency
declared in Executive Order 12722, revoke that Executive Order and Execu-
tive Order 12724 of August 9, 1990, Executive Order 12734 of November
14, 1990, Executive Order 12743 of January 18, 1991, Executive Order 12751
of February 14, 1991, and Executive Order 12817 of October 21, 1992,
that are based on that national emergency. I hereby amend Executive Order
13290 of March 20, 2003, so that the authorities therein remain in effect
based on the national emergency I declared in Executive Order 13303 of
May 22, 2003, and expanded in Executive Order 13315 of August 28, 2003.
At the same time, and in order to take additional steps to deal with the
national emergency that I declared in Executive Order 13303, and expanded
in Executive Order 13315, with respect to the unusual and extraordinary
threat to the national security and foreign policy of the United States posed
by obstacles to the orderly reconstruction of Iraq, the restoration and mainte-
nance of peace and security in that country, and the development of political,
administrative and economic institutions in Iraq, I hereby order:
Section 1. Pursuant to section 202(a) of the NEA (50 U.S.C. 1622(a)), termi-
nation of the national emergency declared in Executive Order 12722 shall
not affect any action taken or proceeding pending but not finally concluded
or determined as of the effective date of this order, any action or proceeding
based on any act committed prior to such date, or any rights or duties
that matured or penalties that were incurred prior to such date. Pursuant
to section 207(a) of IEEPA (50 U.S.C. 1706(a)), and subject to such regulations,
orders, directives, or licenses as may be issued pursuant to this order,
I hereby determine that the continuation of prohibitions with regard to
transactions involving property blocked pursuant to Executive Orders 12722
or 12724 that continues to be blocked as of the effective date of this order
is necessary on account of claims involving Iraq.
Sec. 2. The Annex to Executive Order 13315 is replaced and superseded
in its entirety by the Annex to this order.
Sec. 3. I hereby amend Executive Order 13290 by removing ‘‘the national
emergency declared in Executive Order 12722 of August 2, 1990’’ and replac-
ing it with ‘‘the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13303
of March 20, 2003, and expanded in Executive Order 13315 of August
28, 2003’’.
VerDate jul<14>2003 20:07 Jul 29, 2004 Jkt 203001 PO 00000 Frm 00003 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\FR\FM\30JYE0.SGM 30JYE0
=== PDF page 2 of 13 ===
46056 Federal Register / Vol. 69, No. 146 / Friday, July 30, 2004 / Presidential Documents
Sec. 4. Unless licensed or otherwise authorized pursuant to this order or
otherwise consistent with U.S. law, the trade in or transfer of ownership
or possession of Iraqi cultural property or other items of archeological,
historical, cultural, rare scientific, and religious importance that were illegally
removed, or for which a reasonable suspicion exists that they were illegally
removed, from the Iraq National Museum, the National Library, and other
locations in Iraq since August 6, 1990, is prohibited.
Sec. 5. I hereby determine that the making of donations of the type specified
in section 203(b)(2) of IEEPA (50 U.S.C. 1702(b)(2)) by or to persons deter-
mined to be subject to the sanctions imposed by Executive Order 13315
or by this order would seriously impair my ability to deal with the national
emergency declared in Executive Order 13303, and expanded by Executive
Order 13315, or would endanger the Armed Forces of the United States
that are engaged in hostilities, and I hereby prohibit such donations as
provided in section 1 of Executive Order 13315 as amended by this order.
Sec. 6. For those persons listed in the Annex to this order or determined
to be subject to Executive Order 13315 or this order who might have a
constitutional presence in the United States, I find that because of the
ability to transfer funds or other assets instantaneously, prior notice to
such persons of measures to be taken pursuant to this order would render
these measures ineffectual. I therefore determine that for these measures
to be effective in addressing the national emergency declared in Executive
Order 13303, and expanded by Executive Order 13315, there need be no
prior notice of a listing or determination made pursuant to Executive Order
13315 or this order.
Sec. 7. The Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary
of State, is hereby authorized to take such actions, including the promulgation
of rules and regulations, and to employ all powers granted to the President
by IEEPA and UNPA as may be necessary to carry out the purposes of
this order. The Secretary of the Treasury may redelegate any of these func-
tions to other officers and agencies of the United States Government con-
sistent with applicable law. All agencies of the United States Government
are hereby directed to take all appropriate measures within their authority
to carry out the provisions of this order.
Sec. 8. The Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary
of State, is authorized to determine subsequent to the issuance of the order,
that circumstances no longer warrant the inclusion of a person in the Annex
to this order and that such person is therefore no longer covered within
the scope of the order.
Sec. 9. This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or
benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any
party against the United States, its departments, agencies, instrumentalities,
or entities, officers or employees, or any other person.

Title 3— Executive Order 12439 of Septem ber 8, 1983
The President President’s Task Force on Food A ssistance
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and law s of the
United States of Am erica, in order to establish, in accordance with the
provisions of the Federal Advisory Committee A ct, as amended (5 U.S.C. App.
I), an advisory committee to exam ine programs intended to render food
assistance to the needy and to make recom m endations on how such programs
m ay be improved, it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. Establishm ent, (a) There is established the President’s Task Force
on Food A ssistance, which shall be composed of not more than fifteen
persons, who shall be appointed by the President from among citizens of the
United States who are not full-time officers or employees of the Federal
Government.
(b) The President shall designate a Chairman, and m ay also designate a Vice
Chairman, from among the members of the Task Force.
Sec. 2. Functions.  The Task Force shall analyze Federal and other programs
intended to render food assistance to the needy and shall make recom m enda­
tions to the President and the Secretary of Agriculture with respect to how
such programs m ay be improved. The Task Force shall submit its report to the
President within ninety days of its first meeting.
Sec. 3. Adm inistration, (a) The heads of Executive agencies shall, to the extent
permitted by law, provide the Task Force such information as it m ay require
for purposes of carrying out its functions.
(b) M embers of the Task F oice shall serve without com pensation for their
work on the Task Force, but m ay be allowed travel expenses, including per
diem in lieu of subsistence, as authorized by law  for persons serving intermit­
tently in the Government service (5 U.S.C. 5701-5707), to the extent funds are
available therefor.
(c) The Secretary of Agriculture shall, to the extent permitted by law  and
subject to the availability of funds, provide the Task Force with such adminis­
trative services, facilities, staff and other support services as m ay be neces­
sary for the effective perform ance of its functions.

Text hash 1ecc795ae48c0d796b4705a5c01b8e0b6d6885797458eb9a9f4a52ea700a714d; absolute characters 0–3490; files: jobs/clause-drafts/output/texts/cd-opus_zip-12110-2e4b25b993.txt

```text
Executive Order 12110—Federal Advisory Committees
December 28, 1978
CONTINUANCE OF CERTAIN FEDERAL ADVISORY COMMITTEES
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of the United States of America, and in accordance with the provisions of the Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App. I), it is hereby ordered as follows:
1-101. Each advisory committee listed below is continued until December 31, 1980.
(a) Committee for the Preservation of the White House—Executive Order No. 11145, as amended (Department of the Interior).
(b) President's Commission on White House Fellowships—Executive Order No. 11183, as amended (United States Civil Service Commission).
(c) President's Committee on the National Medal of Science—Executive Order No. 11287, as amended (National Science Foundation).
(d) President's Council on Physical Fitness and Sports—Executive Order No. 11562, as amended (Department of Health, Education, and Welfare).
(e) President's Export Council—Executive Order No. 11753 of December 20, 1973 (Department of Commerce).
(f) President's Committee on Mental Retardation—Executive Order No. 11776 of March 28, 1974 (Department of Health, Education, and Welfare).
(g) Federal Advisory Council on Occupational Safety and Health—Executive Order No. 11807 of September 28, 1974 (Department of Labor).
(h) Presidential Advisory Board on Ambassadorial Appointments, Executive Order No. 11970 of February 5, 1977 (Department of State).
(i) Committee on Selection of Federal Judicial Officers—Executive Order No. 11992 of May 24, 1977 (Department of Justice).
(j) United States Circuit Judge Nominating Commission—Executive Order No. 12059, as amended (Department of Justice).
(k) United States Court of Military Appeals Nominating Commission—Executive Order No. 12063 of June 5, 1978 (Department of Defense).
(1) United States Tax Court Nominating Commission—Executive Order No. 12064 of June 5, 1978 (Department of the Treasury).
(m) Judicial Nominating Commission for the District of Puerto Rico—Executive Order No. 12084, as amended (Department of Justice).
1-102. Notwithstanding the provisions of any other Executive order, the functions of the President under the Federal Advisory Committee Act which are applicable to the committees listed in Section 1-101 of this Order, except that of reporting annually to Congress, shall be performed by the head of the department or agency designated after each committee, in accordance with guidelines and procedures established by the Administrator of General Services.
1-103. The following Executive orders, that established committees which have terminated or whose work is completed, are revoked:
(a) Executive Order No. 11482 of September 22, 1969, establishing a Construction Industry Collective Bargaining Commission.
(b) Executive Order No. 11849 of April 1, 1975, establishing the Collective Bargaining Committee in Construction.
(c) Executive Order No. 11534 of June 4, 1970, establishing the National Council on Organized Crime.
(d) Executive Order No. 11971, as amended, establishing the Committee on Selection of the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation.
(e) Executive Order No. 11973 of February 17, 1977, establishing the President's Commission on Mental Health.
(f) Executive Order No. 11998 of June 27, 1977, establishing the President's Commission on Military Compensation.
1-104. Executive Order No. 11984 is superseded.
1-105. This Order shall be effective December 31, 1978.

```

### Tc84c829b9770d834593f706d

Text hash 7ebb6d0334f2fcf03b6fa67838807cab8f05a7d52523c6b9743a975d1e40e90f; absolute characters 2239–3584; files: jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-12534-continuance-certain-federal-advisory-committees.txt

```text
Sec. 3. The following Executive Orders, which established committees that have terminated or been abolished by statute or whose work is completed, are revoked:

(a) Executive Order No. 12502, establishing the Chemical Warfare Review Commission.

(b) Executive Order No. 12369, establishing the President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government.

(c) Executive Order No. 12395, establishing the International Private Enterprise Task Force.

(d) Executive Order No. 12433, establishing the National Bipartisan Commission on Central America.

(e) Executive Order No. 12335, establishing the National Commission on Social Security Reform.

(f) Executive Order No. 12332, establishing the National Productivity Advisory Committee.

(g) Executive Order No. 12412, establishing the Peace Corps Advisory Council.

(h) Executive Order No. 12426, establishing the President's Committee on Women's Business Ownership.

(i) Executive Order No. 12499, establishing the President's Blue Ribbon Task Group on Nuclear Weapons Program Management.

(j) Executive Order No. 12428, establishing the President's Commission on Industrial Competitiveness.

(k) Executive Order No. 12400, establishing the President's Commission on Strategic Forces.

(1) Executive Order No. 12439, establishing the President's Task Force on Food Assistance.

Executive Order 12686 of August 4, 1989
President’s Commission on Aviation Security and Terrorism
?T y j  *Uihorit?  veste<? in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the
United States of America, and in order to establish a Commission on Aviation
Security and Terrorism, it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. E s ta b lis h m e n t, (a) There is established the President’s Commission
on Aviation Security and Terrorism to review and evaluate policy options in
connection with aviation security, with particular reference to the destruction
on December 21, 1988, of Pan American World A irways Flight 103. The
Commission shall consist of seven members appointed by the President. Two
members shall be Senators, and two shall be Members of the House of
Representatives; they shall represent both parties equally. The President shall
consult with the Majority and Republican Leaders of the Senate and the
Speaker and Minority Leader of the House of Representatives in making
appointments from the Senate and House of Representatives, respectively.
(b) The President shall designate a Chairman from among the members of the
Commission.
Sec. 2. F u n c tio n s , (a) The Commission shall conduct a comprehensive study
and appraisal of practices and policy options with respect to preventing
terrorist acts involving aviation. In conducting this effort, the Commission
shall evaluate the adequacy of existing procedures for aviation security,
compliance therewith, and enforcement thereof. The Commission also shall
review options for handling terrorist threats, including prior notification to the
public. Further, the Commission shall investigate practices, policies, and laws
with respect to the treatment of families of victims of terrorist acts.
(b) Within 6 months of the date of this order, the Commission shall submit a
report to the President, which shall be classified if necessary, containing
findings and recommendations. If the Commission’s report is classified, an
unclassified version shall be prepared for public distribution.
Sec. 3. A d m in is tra tio n , (a) To the extent permitted by law and fully protecting
intelligence sources and methods and the ongoing investigations into the
destruction of Pan Anerican World Airways Flight 103 of December 21,1988,
the beads of executive departments, agencies, and independent instrumental­
ities shall provide the Commission, upon request, with such information as it
may require for purposes of carrying out its functions.
{b) Members of the Commission appointed from among private citizens may
receive compensation for their work on the Commission at the daily rate
specified for GS-18 of the General Schedule. While engaged in the work of the
Commission, members appointed from among private citizens of the United
States may be allowed travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of subsist­
ence, as authorized by law for persons serving intermittently in the Govern­
ment service (5 U.S.C. 5701-5707).
(c) To the extent permitted by law and subject to the availability of appropria­
tions, the Department of Transportation shall, among other Administrative
tunchons, provide the Commission with administrative services, funds, facili­
ties, staff, and other support services necessary for the performance of its
unctions and the Secretary of Transportation shall perform the functions of
¡Ye ^ re81(^ ent un(ier the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended (5
.o.C. App. 2), except that of reporting to the Congress, in accordance with the

(7 ) A s nearly as possible, what programs will cost, when the m oney should be

priorities shall be submitted to the President by A pril 1, 1978.

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the

sooner extended.”.

THE PRESIDENT 14887
EXECUTIVE ORDER 11849
Establishing thie C ollective Bargaining Committee in Construction
The President’s Labor-Management Committee established by Execu­
tive Order No. 11809 was authorized to “encourage the establishment of
labor-management committees (bipartite or tripartite) in particular
sectors or industries as may be appropriate.” That Committee expressed
the view that a committee should appropriately be established in the
construction industry.
An interim labor-management committee on collective bargaining
problems in construction, representative of labor and management orga­
nizations involved in collective bargaining in the industry, has met reg­
ularly since November 1974 to explore the feasibility and details of a
continuing committee.
The recommendations of the interim labor-management committee
have been ratified by the standard national labor and management orga­
nizations engaged in collective bargaining in the industry, and their
representatives have been authorized to participate and serve cm such a
committee.
This Order is required to establish an arrangement and machinery
fear an operating structure with a minimum of government interference
in the furtherance of more effective collective bargaining in the industry.
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me as
President of the United States of America, it is ordered as follows:
Section 1. There is hereby established the Collective Bargaining Com­
mittee in Construction (hereinafter referred1  to as the Committee). The
Committee shall consist of ten labor members and ten management
members appointed by the President. The Secretary of Labor or his
designee shall serve as Chairman. The Director of the Federal Mediation
and Conciliation Service shall participate as a member e rf the Committee.
Additional alternate members may be appointed by the Secretary of
Labor.
Sec. 2. (a) The Committee shall facilitate the collective bargaining
process at local and area levels* assist in providing a data bank of wage
and benefit information* encourage peaceful negotiation of responsible
local and area agreements, facilitate local coordinated bargaining and
larger area bargaining wherever appropriate, and seek to resolve par­
ticular disputes that cannot otherwise be reasonably resolved.
(b) In the furtherance of these objectives the Committee is authorized
to hold conferences; and if it deems appropriate, in particular collective
bargaining disputes or in groups of related disputes, the Committee may
make recommendations to the appropriate standard organizations which
are party to collective bargaining in the construction industry concerning
the provisions of agreements or the structure of collective bargaining.
(c) The Committee shall promote more effective machinery for the
resolution of disputes over the terms of collective bargaining agreements
FEDERAL REGISTER. V O L 40, NO. 65— THURSDAY, APRIL 3, 1975

=== PDF page 12 of 192 ===
14888 THE PRESIDENT
which recognizes the interests of each branch of the industry and pre­
serves existing procedures that have been effective.
Sec. 3. In addition to the foregoing tasks, the Committee shall also:
(a) Review and analyze construction manpower under collective
bargaining agreements, including regional requirements and availabilities
of respective skills for projected needs, and the effectiveness of training,
programs, and, if appropriate, maintain a continuing central data file of
manpower requirements and availabilities by major areas of the country;
(b) Consider measures to reduce the instability of demand for con­
struction labor and to provide more weeks of work per year;
(c) Take measures to increase productivity in the industry under col­
lective bargaining agreements;
(d) Improve further the current wage and benefit data base for con­
struction to facilitate collective bargaining at local and regional levels and
the role of the national organizations in dispute settlements;
(e) Consider the problems for collective bargaining arising from the
activities of separate Federal government agencies as they affect the con­
struction industry;
(f) Consider from time to time such problems in the-construction
industry under collective bargaining as it may deem appropriate; and
(g) Encourage the establishment of comparable joint regional or local
committees on an area basis to the extent it deems appropriate.
Sec. 4. In carrying out its functions, the Committee shall give con­
sideration to long term developments in the construction industry under
collective bargaining agreements and shall seek to develop appropriate
policies in the national interest.
Sec. 5. All executive departments and agencies of the Federal govern­
ment are authorized and directed to cooperate with the Committee and
to furnish such information, personnel and assistance, not inconsistent
with law, as it may require in the performance of its duties.
Sec. 6. The Committee shall make periodic reports to the President.
Standard national labor and management organizations are encouraged
to review the operation of the Committee and report to the President
annually on the extent to which the purposes of this Order are being
achieved.
T h e W h ite H ouse ,
April 1, 1975.
[FR Doc.75-8791 Filed 4-1-75 ;2:49 pm]
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 40, NO. 65— THURSDAY, APRIL 3, 1975

Executive Order 13102 of September 25, 1998
Further Amendment to Executive Order 13038, Advisory
Committee on Public Interest Obligations of Digital Television

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the
laws of the United States of America, and in order to extend the reporting
deadline of the Advisory Committee on Public Interest Obligations of Digital
Television Broadcasters, it is hereby ordered that Executive Order 13038,
as previously amended, is further amended by deleting ‘‘October 1, 1998’’
in section 2 and inserting ‘‘December 31, 1998’’ in lieu thereof.

Executive Order 12487 of September 14, 1984
Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the
United States of America, and in accordance with section 2207 of the Deficit
Reduction Act of 1984 (Public Law 98-369), it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. Executive Order No. 12456 of December 30, 1983, as amended, is
further amended by replacing Schedule 8 attached thereto with the corre­
sponding new Schedule 8 attached hereto.
Sec. 2. The adjustments of rates of pay made by section 1 of this Order are
effective on the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or
after January 1,1984.

Title 3—The President
Executive Order 11931 August 3, 1976
Extending Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities to Permanent Observers to the
Organization of American States and to Members of Their Diplomatic Staffs
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Act of November 7, 1973 (87 Stat.
560; 22 U.S.G. 288g), and as President of the United States of America, I extend to
Permanent Observers to the Organization of American States, and to the members of
the diplomatic staffs of such Permanent Observers, the same privileges and immunities,
subject to corresponding conditions and obligations, as are enjoyed'by' diplomatic
envoys accredited to the United States.
This Executive order shall be effective as of November 7, 1973. The enjoyment
of privileges and immunities extended hereunder shall be subject to any Agreements
entered into between the Government of the United States and the Organization of
American States after that date.
T h e W h it e H o u se,
August 3,1976.
[FR Doc.76-22978 Filed 8-3-76;4:50 pm]

Executive Order 12447 of October 27, 1983
President’ s Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the
Federal Government
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the
United States of America, including the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as
amended (5 U.S.C. App. I), and in order to extend the life of the President’s
Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government, it is hereby
ordered that Section 4(b) of Executive Order No. 12369 of June 30, 1982, as
amended, is further amended to read:
“The Committee shall terminate on December 31, 1983, unless sooner ex­
tended.”.

Presidential Documents
4829
Federal Register
Vol. 60, No. 15
Tuesday, January 24, 1995
Title 3—
The President
Executive Order 12946 of January 20, 1995
President’s Advisory Board on Arms Proliferation Policy
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the
laws of the United States of America, including section 1601 of the National
Defense Authorization Act, Fiscal Year 1994 (Public Law 103–160), and
the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended (5 U.S.C. App. 2) (‘‘Act’’),
except that subsections (e) and (f) of section 10 of such Act do not apply,
and section 301 of title 3, United States Code, it is hereby ordered as
follows:
Section 1. Establishment. There is established within the Department of
Defense the ‘‘President’s Advisory Board on Arms Proliferation Policy’’
(‘‘Board’’). The Board shall consist of five members who shall be appointed
by the President from among persons in private life who are noted for
their stature and expertise regarding the proliferation of strategic and ad-
vanced conventional weapons and are from diverse backgrounds. The Presi-
dent shall designate one of the members as Chairperson of the Board.
Sec. 2. Functions. The Board shall advise the President on implementation
of United States conventional arms transfer policy, other issues related to
arms proliferation policy, and on other matters deemed appropriate by the
President. The Board shall report to the President through the Assistant
to the President for National Security Affairs.
Sec. 3. Administration. (a) The heads of executive agencies shall, to the
extent permitted by law, provide to the Board such information as it may
require for the purpose of carrying out its functions.
(b) Members of the Board shall serve without compensation, but shall
be allowed travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of subsistence, as
authorized by law, including 5 U.S.C. 5701–5707 and section 7(d) of the
Act, for persons serving intermittently in government service.
(c) The Department of Defense or the head of any other Federal department
or agency may detail to the Board, upon request of the Chairperson of
the Board, any of the personnel of the department or agency to assist
the Board in carrying out its duties.
(d) The Secretary of Defense shall designate a federally funded research
and development center with expertise in the matters covered by the Board
to provide the Board with such support services as the Board may need
to carry out its duties.
(e) The Department of Defense shall provide the Board with administrative
services, facilities, staff, and other support services necessary for the perform-
ance of its functions.
Sec. 4. General. (a) The Board shall terminate 30 days after the date on
which the President submits the final report of the Board to the Congress.
(b) For reasons of national security or for such other reasons as specified
in section 552(b) of title 5, United States Code, the Board shall not provide
public notice or access to meetings at which national security information
will be discussed. Authority to make such determinations shall reside with
the Secretary of Defense or his designee who must be an official required
to be appointed by and with the advice and consent of the Senate.
(c) Information made available to the Board shall be given all necessary
security protection in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
=== PDF page 2 of 2 ===
4830 Federal Register / Vol. 60, No. 15 / Tuesday, January 24, 1995 / Presidential Documents
(d) Each member of the Board and each member of the Board’s staff
shall execute an agreement not to reveal any classified information obtained
by virtue of his or her service with the Board except as authorized by
applicable law and regulations.
œ–
THE WHITE HOUSE,
January 20, 1995.
[FR Doc. 95–1925
Filed 1–20–95; 5:01pm]

11708 (March 23, 1973; 38 FR 7979-7980, held official FR scan text) placed fourteen positions in level IV (Sec. 1), continued eight in level V (Sec. 2) and revoked EO 11248 except for the Sec. 2 positions (Sec. 3). Sec. 1 and Sec. 2 were amended item by item by EO 11715 (April 24, 1973), EO 11727 Sec. 4 (deleting items (6) and (7), effective as of July 1, 1973 under its Sec. 6) and EO 11736 (August 6, 1973); these are partial amendments recorded as later events, not ends of the clauses, which continued as amended. EO 11768 of February 20, 1974, Sec. 4, superseded 'Executive Order No. 11708 of March 23, 1973, as amended'; it states no effective date, so Sec. 1 and Sec. 2 first end on February 20, 1974, the whole-order end. Sec. 3 operated once on issuance and is recorded as spent on March 23, 1973. The draft's QUARANTINED_RELATIONSHIP_CONFLICT (Stage 19 causal queue) is resolved: its four live leads are exactly the EO 11715, 11727 and 11736 amendments and the EO 11768 supersession read here, and its ten quarantined leads (EOs 11389, 11393, 11409, 11441, 11581, 11587, 11604, 11634, 11676, 11699, flagged PREDECESSOR_NOT_EARLIER_THAN_ACTOR) are orders issued before EO 11708 (most of them amendments of EO 11248), which cannot act on a later order; none ends EO 11708 earlier. The 21 U.S.C. 801 note hit is the printed text of EO 11727. OFR 1989 table: 'Amended by EOs 11715, 11727, 11736. 11812 (Oct. 7, 1974, 'shall take effect October 1, 1974'; 39 FR 36307-36312) adjusts for members of the uniformed services the monthly basic pay (Sec. 1 tables), basic allowance for subsistence (Sec. 2) and basic allowance for quarters (Sec. 3), caps basic pay at Executive Schedule level V under 5 U.S.C. 5308 (Sec. 4), supersedes seven earlier uniformed-pay orders (Sec. 5) and sets its effective date (Sec. 6). It has no term of its own; its rates govern until the next adjustment. EO 11883 (signed Oct. 6, 1975) sec. 5 supersedes 'Executive Order No. 11812 of October 7, 1974', and its sec. 2 replacement rates for basic pay, subsistence and quarters 'shall be effective on October 1, 1975' (sec. 4). Every clause except Sec. 5 therefore first ended on 1975-10-01, the stated effective date in the acting instrument (the displacement was retroactive from that date to Oct. 6). Sec. 5's supersession of earlier orders was completed when the order issued on 1974-10-07 (spent). Whole-order end = 1975-10-01. All of this order concerns the uniformed services, so the agency-specific civilian pay-period dates in EO 11883 sec. 4 do not affect it. Counterevidence: the U.S. Code note under 37 U.S.C. 1009 states that EO 11812 'which provided for the adjustment of pay rates effective Oct. 1, 1974, was superseded by Ex. Ord. No. 11883' (history, not a predicate); the 1989 Codification row reads 'Superseded by EO 11883'. CONFLICT QUARANTINED_RELATIONSHIP_CONFLICT resolved: the quarantined relationship (research/stage15/AUDIT/RELATIONSHIP_CHRONOLOGY_VIOLATIONS.csv) is an OFR note on EO 11778 (Apr. 12, 1974) reading 'Amends: EO 11692, December 15, 1972 (which was revoked by EO 11812, October 7, 1974)'; the parenthetical names this order as the later superseder of EO 11692, it is not an event on this order, and the Stage 15 audit already suppressed it. adjusts statutory pay systems (s.1, Schedules 1-3), uniformed-services pay and allowances (s.2, Schedule 4) and executive, congressional and judicial salaries (s.3, Schedules 5-7), sets effective dates (s.4) and supersedes EO 11883 (s.5). Each schedule is inventoried as its own clause (heading quoted; the tables themselves are the operative rates). EO 11943 (October 25, 1976) corrected one figure in Schedule 3 (later event). EO 12010 of September 28, 1977 (42 FR 52365, read in full) section 4: 'Executive Order No. 11941 of October 1, 1976, is superseded', so every clause is terminated, but its rates take effect on pay-period dates that the held sources do not fix, and it does not cover Schedules 5-7. The current-law lead (28 U.S.C. 172 note) is a historical salary note ('formerly set out as a note under section 5332 of Title 5'), not a continuing basis, so it does not contradict the NO status. No first-end date is asserted. chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"Executive Order 12110—Federal Advisory Committees\nDecember 28, 1978\nCONTINUANCE OF CERTAIN FEDERAL ADVISORY COMMITTEES\nBy the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of the United States of America, and in accordance with the provisions of the Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App. I), it is hereby ordered as follows:\n1-101. Each advisory committee listed below is continued until December 31, 1980.\n(a) Committee for the Preservation of the White House—Executive Order No. 11145, as amended (Department of the Interior).\n(b) President's Commission on White House Fellowships—Executive Order No. 11183, as amended (United States Civil Service Commission).\n(c) President's Committee on the National Medal of Science—Executive Order No. 11287, as amended (National Science Foundation).\n(d) President's Council on Physical Fitness and Sports—Executive Order No. 11562, as amended (Department of Health, Education, and Welfare).\n(e) President's Export Council—Executive Order No. 11753 of December 20, 1973 (Department of Commerce).\n(f) President's Committee on Mental Retardation—Executive Order No. 11776 of March 28, 1974 (Department of Health, Education, and Welfare).\n(g) Federal Advisory Council on Occupational Safety and Health—Executive Order No. 11807 of September 28, 1974 (Department of Labor).\n(h) Presidential Advisory Board on Ambassadorial Appointments, Executive Order No. 11970 of February 5, 1977 (Department of State).\n(i) Committee on Selection of Federal Judicial Officers—Executive Order No. 11992 of May 24, 1977 (Department of Justice).\n(j) United States Circuit Judge Nominating Commission—Executive Order No. 12059, as amended (Department of Justice).\n(k) United States Court of Military Appeals Nominating Commission—Executive Order No. 12063 of June 5, 1978 (Department of Defense).\n(1) United States Tax Court Nominating Commission—Executive Order No. 12064 of June 5, 1978 (Department of the Treasury).\n(m) Judicial Nominating Commission for the District of Puerto Rico—Executive Order No. 12084, as amended (Department of Justice).\n1-102. Notwithstanding the provisions of any other Executive order, the functions of the President under the Federal Advisory Committee Act which are applicable to the committees listed in Section 1-101 of this Order, except that of reporting annually to Congress, shall be performed by the head of the department or agency designated after each committee, in accordance with guidelines and procedures established by the Administrator of General Services.\n1-103. The following Executive orders, that established committees which have terminated or whose work is completed, are revoked:\n(a) Executive Order No. 11482 of September 22, 1969, establishing a Construction Industry Collective Bargaining Commission.\n(b) Executive Order No. 11849 of April 1, 1975, establishing the Collective Bargaining Committee in Construction.\n(c) Executive Order No. 11534 of June 4, 1970, establishing the National Council on Organized Crime.\n(d) Executive Order No. 11971, as amended, establishing the Committee on Selection of the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation.\n","sections_touched":["Section 1"],"signing_date":"1978-12-28","source":{"acceptable_as_original":false,"filing_date":null,"grade":"mirror_transcription","instrument_id":"EO:12110","page_or_item":"American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition)","requires_page_check":false,"sha256":"2e4b25b9939fbd640b4fb77f76190f025f039f0714bf80b0c6ccf790b9b22b04","signing_date":"1978-12-28","text_path":"jobs/clause-drafts/output/texts/cd-opus_zip-12110-2e4b25b993.txt","text_sha256":"1ecc795ae48c0d796b4705a5c01b8e0b6d6885797458eb9a9f4a52ea700a714d","url":"https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/executive-order-12110-federal-advisory-committees"},"verb":"revoke"},{"actor_id":"EO:12110","char_end":3114,"char_start":2503,"confidence":"medium","how_named":"direct","id":"CHAIN:EO:11971#6","notes":"Change wording lead; chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"1-103. All other clauses depended on the Committee's existence, which ended under the order's own terms at a date not recorded in held sources, or, if extended, no later than EO 12110's revocation effective December 31, 1978. {"confidence":"medium","events":[{"actor_id":"EO:12110","char_end":3272,"char_start":0,"confidence":"medium","how_named":"direct","id":"CHAIN:EO:11973#1","notes":"Change wording lead; chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"Executive Order 12110—Federal Advisory Committees\nDecember 28, 1978\nCONTINUANCE OF CERTAIN FEDERAL ADVISORY COMMITTEES\nBy the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of the United States of America, and in accordance with the provisions of the Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App. I), it is hereby ordered as follows:\n1-101. Each advisory committee listed below is continued until December 31, 1980.\n(a) Committee for the Preservation of the White House—Executive Order No. 11145, as amended (Department of the Interior).\n(b) President's Commission on White House Fellowships—Executive Order No. 11183, as amended (United States Civil Service Commission).\n(c) President's Committee on the National Medal of Science—Executive Order No. 11287, as amended (National Science Foundation).\n(d) President's Council on Physical Fitness and Sports—Executive Order No. 11562, as amended (Department of Health, Education, and Welfare).\n(e) President's Export Council—Executive Order No. 11753 of December 20, 1973 (Department of Commerce).\n(f) President's Committee on Mental Retardation—Executive Order No. 11776 of March 28, 1974 (Department of Health, Education, and Welfare).\n(g) Federal Advisory Council on Occupational Safety and Health—Executive Order No. 11807 of September 28, 1974 (Department of Labor).\n(h) Presidential Advisory Board on Ambassadorial Appointments, Executive Order No. 11970 of February 5, 1977 (Department of State).\n(i) Committee on Selection of Federal Judicial Officers—Executive Order No. 11992 of May 24, 1977 (Department of Justice).\n(j) United States Circuit Judge Nominating Commission—Executive Order No. 12059, as amended (Department of Justice).\n(k) United States Court of Military Appeals Nominating Commission—Executive Order No. 12063 of June 5, 1978 (Department of Defense).\n(1) United States Tax Court Nominating Commission—Executive Order No. 12064 of June 5, 1978 (Department of the Treasury).\n(m) Judicial Nominating Commission for the District of Puerto Rico—Executive Order No. 12084, as amended (Department of Justice).\n1-102. Notwithstanding the provisions of any other Executive order, the functions of the President under the Federal Advisory Committee Act which are applicable to the committees listed in Section 1-101 of this Order, except that of reporting annually to Congress, shall be performed by the head of the department or agency designated after each committee, in accordance with guidelines and procedures established by the Administrator of General Services.\n1-103. The following Executive orders, that established committees which have terminated or whose work is completed, are revoked:\n(a) Executive Order No. 11482 of September 22, 1969, establishing a Construction Industry Collective Bargaining Commission.\n(b) Executive Order No. 11849 of April 1, 1975, establishing the Collective Bargaining Committee in Construction.\n(c) Executive Order No. 11534 of June 4, 1970, establishing the National Council on Organized Crime.\n(d) Executive Order No. 11971, as amended, establishing the Committee on Selection of the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation.\n(e) Executive Order No. 11973 of February 17, 1977, establishing the President's Commission on Mental Health.\n","sections_touched":["Section 1"],"signing_date":"1978-12-28","source":{"acceptable_as_original":false,"filing_date":null,"grade":"mirror_transcription","instrument_id":"EO:12110","page_or_item":"American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition)","requires_page_check":false,"sha256":"2e4b25b9939fbd640b4fb77f76190f025f039f0714bf80b0c6ccf790b9b22b04","signing_date":"1978-12-28","text_path":"jobs/clause-drafts/output/texts/cd-opus_zip-12110-2e4b25b993.txt","text_sha256":"1ecc795ae48c0d796b4705a5c01b8e0b6d6885797458eb9a9f4a52ea700a714d","url":"https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/executive-order-12110-federal-advisory-committees"},"verb":"revoke"},{"actor_id":"EO:12110","char_end":3225,"char_start":2503,"confidence":"medium","how_named":"direct","id":"CHAIN:EO:11973#2","notes":"Change wording lead; chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"1-103. EO 12110 (effective 1978-12-31) describes it as terminated or its work completed.","whole_order_end not set until the transmittal date is established (latest possible date 1978-12-31)."],"research_rationale":"EO 11973 (February 17, 1977; 42 FR 10677-10678, read in the held govinfo scan) established the President's Commission on Mental Health (secs. 1-9). Sec. 9 makes it terminate sixty days after it transmits its final report, which sec. 3 required by April 1, 1978. EO 12110 sec. 1-103(e) later revoked the order, effective December 31, 1978, as one whose committee had 'terminated' or whose work was 'completed'; the revocation is therefore a clean-up after the termination under sec. 9. Because the transmittal date is not in held sources and must not be inferred from the deadline, the first ends and the whole-order end are left open. The Commission was within the two-year limit of the Federal Advisory Committee Act, so no statutory termination intervened. Savings: none App. I), it is hereby ordered as follows:\n1-101. Each advisory committee listed below is continued until December 31, 1980.\n(a) Committee for the Preservation of the White House—Executive Order No. 11145, as amended (Department of the Interior).\n(b) President's Commission on White House Fellowships—Executive Order No. 11183, as amended (United States Civil Service Commission).\n(c) President's Committee on the National Medal of Science—Executive Order No. 11287, as amended (National Science Foundation).\n(d) President's Council on Physical Fitness and Sports—Executive Order No. 11562, as amended (Department of Health, Education, and Welfare).\n(e) President's Export Council—Executive Order No. 11753 of December 20, 1973 (Department of Commerce).\n(f) President's Committee on Mental Retardation—Executive Order No. 11776 of March 28, 1974 (Department of Health, Education, and Welfare).\n(g) Federal Advisory Council on Occupational Safety and Health—Executive Order No. 11807 of September 28, 1974 (Department of Labor).\n(h) Presidential Advisory Board on Ambassadorial Appointments, Executive Order No. 11970 of February 5, 1977 (Department of State).\n(i) Committee on Selection of Federal Judicial Officers—Executive Order No. 11992 of May 24, 1977 (Department of Justice).\n(j) United States Circuit Judge Nominating Commission—Executive Order No. 12059, as amended (Department of Justice).\n(k) United States Court of Military Appeals Nominating Commission—Executive Order No. 12063 of June 5, 1978 (Department of Defense).\n(1) United States Tax Court Nominating Commission—Executive Order No. 12064 of June 5, 1978 (Department of the Treasury).\n(m) Judicial Nominating Commission for the District of Puerto Rico—Executive Order No. 12084, as amended (Department of Justice).\n1-102. Notwithstanding the provisions of any other Executive order, the functions of the President under the Federal Advisory Committee Act which are applicable to the committees listed in Section 1-101 of this Order, except that of reporting annually to Congress, shall be performed by the head of the department or agency designated after each committee, in accordance with guidelines and procedures established by the Administrator of General Services.\n1-103. The following Executive orders, that established committees which have terminated or whose work is completed, are revoked:\n(a) Executive Order No. 11482 of September 22, 1969, establishing a Construction Industry Collective Bargaining Commission.\n(b) Executive Order No. 11849 of April 1, 1975, establishing the Collective Bargaining Committee in Construction.\n(c) Executive Order No. 11534 of June 4, 1970, establishing the National Council on Organized Crime.\n(d) Executive Order No. 11971, as amended, establishing the Committee on Selection of the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation.\n(e) Executive Order No. 11973 of February 17, 1977, establishing the President's Commission on Mental Health.\n(f) Executive Order No. 11998 of June 27, 1977, establishing the President's Commission on Military Compensation.\n1-104. Executive Order No. 11984 is superseded.\n1-105. The order has no sunset, termination or report clause. The machine own-term kinds ('condition' and an undated 'fixed_term', plus a quoted conflict) are all noise: they were picked up from other documents printed on the same Federal Register pages (the public-inspection notice, a list of rules going into effect, and a Governors' proclamation), not from the order. EO 12154 (signed 1979-09-04, 44 FR 51965, held FR text, read in full; reading record LSP-EO_12154) sec. 1-202 revokes it 'as amended' with no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing. Three orders amended EO 12076 before that and were read in full: EO 12099 (1978-11-17) moves the Director of Policy Review, Department of Defense, from level V (item 1-102(e)) to level IV (new item (r)); EO 12111 (1979-01-02) deletes the Interior position in item 1-102(g) and adds a Commerce position as (s); EO 12119 (1979-02-14) deletes the Justice position in item 1-101(f) and inserts a Treasury position. Those three items therefore have an earlier first end than the revocation (1-102(e) on 1978-11-17, 1-102(g) on 1979-01-02, 1-101(f) on 1979-02-14), and the two list leads carry all three amendments as later events; every other clause ends with the revocation. Inventory correction: the dossier's 31 item clauses mis-bound items (q) and (n-dup2) and omit secs. 1-201 and 1-202 (see inventory_overrides, 35 clauses). 48 FR 377, Federal Register of January 5, 1983) was read in full in the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12398.txt. It amends Executive Order 12369 (President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government): the lead recital and instruction (to increase the membership and extend the life of the Survey), subsection (a) (the Committee is composed of not more than 170 members appointed by the President from among citizens in private life) and subsection (b) (section 4(b) restated so that, in accordance with the Federal Advisory Committee Act, the Committee terminates on June 30, 1983, unless sooner extended). The dossier evidence for the EO 12553 revocation was re-read against the held EO 12553 text, whose revocation table lists 12398. Later orders read in their held Federal Register texts and recorded as later events of subsection (b): EO 12429 (signed 1983-06-28) restates section 4(b) with the date October 30, 1983; EO 12447 (signed 1983-10-27) with December 31, 1983; EO 12455 (signed 1983-12-29) with January 31, 1984, each unless sooner extended. EO 12534 (signed 1985-09-30; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12534.txt, sha256 2f7a5c13126573ec9fb7f10631df9e25cac3065f405355c469a0222363ab443c) revokes, in section 3(b), Executive Order No. 12369 establishing the President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government, among orders that established committees that have terminated or been abolished by statute or whose work is completed; its section 5 reads \"Sec. 5 This Order shall be effective September 30,1985.\" It names the parent order (without the words as amended) but not this amending order, so under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments it is a disclosed earlier candidate end (1985-09-30), not the end. Bounded search: the dossier's three machine searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts); the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; full reads of EO 12553, EO 12429, EO 12447, EO 12455 and EO 12534 in their held FR texts. the first end of every clause (and so whole_order_end) is not established. Sec. 4(b) ends the Task Force thirty days after it submitted its report, and in no event later than January 31, 1984; the outer limit is known, the actual date is not. No held source records the date the report was actually submitted, and a reporting deadline is not evidence of that date. EO 12534 sec. 3 (effective 1985-09-30) is a cleanup revocation of a body it describes as already terminated, so it cannot be used as the first end. Needed: an official record of the report's transmittal date (for example the Weekly Compilation of Presidential Documents or the report itself), queued through FETCH_QUEUE.jsonl."],"research_rationale":"EO 12439 (Sept. 8, 1983; 48 FR 40871) established the President's Task Force on Food Assistance under FACA; its eight operative subsections all concern the Task Force. Section 4(b) ends it 'thirty days after submission of its report to the President, but in no event later than January 31, 1984'; the report was due within ninety days of the first meeting (sec. 2). No amendment exists. The Task Force therefore ended on or before January 31, 1984, but the exact date depends on when the report was submitted (if more than thirty days before January 31, 1984, the end is earlier), which no held source records. Every clause is terminated; the first-end date is left open rather than set to the outer limit. The draft's FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT is resolved by reading EO 12534 sec. 3, which revokes each listed order as a whole; the 'partial' reading came only from the OFR catalog's acting-order phrasing 'Revokes advisory committees established by'. first end not established. The order's own term (sec. 4(b)) and the EO 12534 sec. 3(i) revocation both fall on 1985-09-30, but Pub. L. 98-525 sec. 1632 (98 Stat.), under which the Task Group was established, is not held; read it for an earlier statutory termination (for example on submission of the report due July 15, 1985) before recording 1985-09-30 as the first end."],"research_rationale":"EO 12499 (Jan. 18, 1985; 50 FR 2947) established the President's Blue Ribbon Task Group on Nuclear Weapons Program Management under Pub. L. 98-525 sec. 1632 and FACA; its nine operative subsections all concern the Task Group. Section 4(b): 'The Task Group shall terminate on September 30,1985, unless its existence is sooner extended in accordance with the Federal Advisory Committee Act'; EO 12534 sec. 3(i) revoked the order effective the same day. So under the order itself every clause ended no later than September 30, 1985. The claim stops short of that date because the Task Group was created to carry out a statutory mandate (report due by July 15, 1985, sec. 2(b)) and the statute is not held: if sec. 1632 ended the Task Group on reporting, the first end is earlier. EO 12534 sec. 3's heading (committees 'terminated or ... abolished by statute or whose work is completed') does not settle it. The draft's FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT is resolved by reading EO 12534 sec. 3, which revokes each listed order as a whole; the 'partial' reading came only from the OFR catalog's acting-order phrasing 'Revokes advisory committees established by'. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.","rationale":"I read the complete held EO 12686 (54 FR 32629, Aug. 4, 1989): it establishes the President's Commission on Aviation Security and Terrorism (Pan Am 103), sets functions, a report within 6 months (sec. 2(b)), administration under DOT and FACA, and in sec. 4 provides that 'The Commission shall terminate 30 days after submitting its report to the President.' It has no savings clause. I read the held EO 12774 (56 FR 49833, Sept. 27, 1991), secs. 3-5: sec. 3, headed as revoking orders 'which established committees that have been terminated or whose work has been completed', lists '(b) Executive Order No. 12686, as amended by Executive Order No. 12705, establishing the President's Commission on Aviation Security and Terrorism', and sec. 5 makes the order effective Sept. 30, 1991. This is an express revocation of the whole order naming it by number, with no carve-out and no savings language. EO 12705 (March 3, 1990) extended the report deadline to May 15, 1990, so under sec. 4 the Commission would have terminated by its own term about 30 days after the report (the date the report was submitted is not held), which would be an earlier ending than the 1991 revocation; I did not use the report deadline as a basis and the sec. 4 own-term evidence is held only in an APP copy. The catalog note ('Amended by EO 12705; Revoked by EO 12774') and its candidate events agree but are leads; the basis is the held acting text. 4, 1989, President’s Commission on Aviation Security and Terrorism, matching the census register row (1989-08-04). Text and inventory: the machine inventory has six scopes and stops inside section 3(c) at a page break, leaving out the rest of 3(c), section 3(d) and section 4 (the termination sentence). I corrected the inventory: section 3(c) now runs to the end of its sentence, section 3(d) and section 4 are added as scopes, and the other spans are kept (all spans in the registered text). All clauses belong to one advisory commission. Ending: Executive Order 12774 section 3(b) revokes Executive Order 12686, as amended by Executive Order 12705, effective September 30, 1991 (section 5). The report deadline in section 2(b) and the report-relative termination in section 4 are not ends (owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines). Original grade: Federal Register machine text.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Candidate earlier ends examined. (3) A search of the held corpus for the number 12686 found the amending order, Executive Order 12774 and the order's own texts; the OFR disposition-note machine search lists two hits. Executive Order 12774 is the only instrument that revokes the order.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"The order has no command that outlives the Commission: the information, compensation, administrative-support and Federal Advisory Committee Act provisions serve only the Commission.\",\"savings_check\":\"Executive Order 12774 has no wording preserving the Commission or its work: section 1 continues other committees, section 2 reassigns Federal Advisory Committee Act functions only for those, and section 3 revokes this order without exception; sections 1 through 5 were read.\",\"scope_check\":\"All eight clauses (six machine scopes, one enlarged, plus sections 3(d) and 4) end by the same revocation. That event and its effective-date provision are now cited to the official Federal Register text of EO 13286 (68 FR 10619, March 5, 2003; sections 35 and 92 are the supplement excerpts); the mechanism is unchanged (a partial amendment, not an end). EO 12743 of January 18, 1991 (56 FR 2661, Federal Register of January 23, 1991; held official Federal Register text layer, read in full from the heading to the signature date line) orders Ready Reserve call-ups and invokes suspension authorities in seven sections: section 1 (10 U.S.C. 673 call-up authority), sections 2 and 3 (10 U.S.C. 527 and 644 suspension authorities), section 4 (delegation to the Secretary of Defense), section 5 (redelegation), section 6 (no private right) and section 7 (effective immediately and transmittal). The inventory of seven sections is complete. The preamble cites the National Emergencies Act and section 301 of title 3 and recites that the order is in furtherance of Executive Order 12722. It has no term or sunset. EO 13350 (69 FR 46055, Federal Register of July 30, 2004) revokes it by name in its preamble, effective 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on July 30, 2004 (section 10). Section 1 of EO 13350 preserves, under section 202(a) of the National Emergencies Act, actions taken, proceedings pending, acts committed and rights or duties that matured or penalties incurred before the effective date, and continues under section 207(a) of IEEPA the prohibitions on property blocked under Executive Orders 12722 or 12724; its sections 2-8 deal with the 2003 emergency (Executive Orders 13303 and 13315, 13290), and its section 9 disclaims private rights. It transfers no function of EO 12743. Earlier-end test: the packet's by-number lookup of held order texts finds Executive Order 12743 cited only in the texts of EO 13286 (section 35) and EO 13350; the three machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR/CFR as of 2026-10-14, and the Federal Register order catalog) record the same two events, the U.S. Code hit being an editorial note printed under 10 U.S.C. 12302. No order suspended or ended any section before 2004-07-30; the EO 13286 amendment ended nothing. All seven sections first ended on 2004-07-30, which is the whole-order end. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (see savings).\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Each section's first end is the express revocation by EO 13350, effective 2004-07-30. The order has no own end date, sunset, report deadline or condition. EO 13286 section 35 (effective 2003-03-01) is an amendment and ends nothing; the packet's by-number lookup of held texts, the Federal Register order catalog and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches show no suspension, revocation or supersession of any section before 2004-07-30. The revocation reaches the order because EO 13350 names it and states the reason (it is based on the terminated Iraq emergency); it is not a general rule applied by default.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"No section stands on a command independent of the order: the call-up and suspension authorities are statutory powers (10 U.S.C. 673, 527, 644) that the order only invoked and delegated, and the order creates no office, fund, property or private right. The revocation of the order does not purport to repeal those statutes. EO 13350 does not except any revoked order from its revocation.\",\"savings_check\":\"Completed effects are preserved: EO 13350 section 1 states, under section 202(a) of the National Emergencies Act, that termination of the Iraq emergency 'shall not affect any action taken or proceeding pending but not finally concluded or determined as of the effective date of this order, any action or proceeding based on any act committed prior to such date, or any rights or duties that matured or penalties that were incurred prior to such date'. Call-ups to active duty ordered, service performed and suspensions applied before 2004-07-30 are such actions; EO 13350 has no savings clause naming EO 12743 specifically.\",\"scope_check\":\"All seven numbered sections are inventoried: sections 1-5 are operative (invocation of call-up authority, two suspension authorities, one delegation, one redelegation), section 6 is a no-right statement and section 7 states effectiveness and transmittal. The preamble is a recital of authority, not an operative clause. EO 13350 revokes the order as a whole by name, so every section ends 12743 (signed 1991-01-18, 56 FR 2661-2662), read in full from the held official FR text: preamble (NEA sec. 301; in furtherance of the EO 12722 emergency); sec. 1 invokes 10 U.S.C. 673 for the Secretaries concerned; secs. 2-3 invoke 10 U.S.C. 527 and 644; sec. 4 delegates the 527/644 authority to the Secretary of Defense; sec. 5 redelegation; sec. 6 no private rights; sec. 7 effective immediately and transmittal. It has no term or sunset. EO 13350 (preamble) revokes it in full as an order based on the EO 12722 emergency, effective 12:01 a.m. EDT 2004-07-30 (sec. 10). The dossier's 7 clauses cover secs. 1-7 with no textual gap. D6 / earlier-end test: the by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts finds 12743 named as an order only in EO 13286 sec. 35 and EO 13350 (the other hits are pay-table figures and FR page numbers in EO 8280, 8281, 9490, 9491, 9793, 12165, 12199, 12200); OFR catalog notes record the EO 13286 amendment and the EO 13350 revocation, and the USC note at 10 U.S.C. 12302 records the same two events. The EO 13286 sec. 35 amendment (effective 2003-03-01) is attached as a later event on sec. 1; it substitutes Homeland Security for Transportation and ends nothing. Reading EO 12964 (60 FR 33095) and EO 12987 (61 FR 4205) in full shows that this is the report deadline in sec. 2(a). The dossier's single clause covers the whole operative text. - **ACT:EO:13038>EO:13138@85bd7ce11b3e3224**; S8bbf2ed07ba862b2fc707173; {"actor_id":"EO:13138","char_end":4270,"char_start":3716,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"stated_date","effective_date":"1999-09-30","effective_wording":[{"char_end":7903,"char_start":6921,"text":"The Committee shall initiate and\nassist in the development of (i) ways to promote public understanding\nand appreciation of the arts and the humanities; (ii) ways to promote private\nsector support for the arts and humanities; (iii) ways to evaluate the effective-\nness of Federal support for the arts and humanities and their relationship\nwith the private sector; (iv) the planning and coordination of appropriate\nparticipation (including productions and projects) in major national cultural\nevents, including the Millennium; (v) activities that incorporate the arts\nand the humanities in government objectives; and (vi) ways to promote\nthe recognition of excellence in the fields of the arts and the humanities.’’;\nand\n(c) in section 3(b), add the following sentence after the first sentence:\n‘‘Private funds accepted under the National Endowment for the Arts’ or\nthe National Endowment for the Humanities’ gift authority may also be\nused to pay expenses of the Committee.’’\nSec. 8."},{"char_end":8438,"char_start":8386,"text":"This order shall be effective September 30, 1999.\nœ–"}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:13038>EO:13138@85bd7ce11b3e3224","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. sha256 5137548d...), headed Executive Order 13075 of February 19, 1998, Special Oversight Board for Department of Defense Investigations of Gulf War Chemical and Biological Incidents, matching the census register row (1998-02-19). Text and inventory: thirteen scopes cover sections 1 through 4(c) to the signature; I confirm the inventory. All clauses belong to one advisory board. Ending: Executive Order 13225 section 3(e) revokes Executive Order 13075, effective September 30, 2001 (section 5). The report deadlines in section 2(e) and the report-relative termination in section 4(b) are not ends (owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines). Original grade: Federal Register machine text.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) Section 4(b) ends the Board 30 days after its final report; no held source dates it, so no own-terms end is claimed (owner ruling of 2026-10-21). (2) The 9-month and 18-month report deadlines are deadlines, not ends. (3) A search of the held corpus for the number 13075 found only Executive Order 13225 and the order's own texts; the OFR disposition-note machine search lists one hit.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"The order has no command that outlives the Board: the information, expense, funding and Federal Advisory Committee Act provisions serve only the Board.\",\"savings_check\":\"Executive Order 13225 has no wording preserving the Board or its work: section 1 continues other committees, section 2 reassigns Federal Advisory Committee Act functions only for those, section 3 revokes this order without exception and section 4 supersedes part of Executive Order 13138.\",\"scope_check\":\"All thirteen clauses end by the same revocation. read.\"}","review_dependency_issues":[],"reviews":[],"scopes":[{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:13075#sec1"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:13075#sec1"},{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:13075#sec1-b"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:13075#sec1-b"},{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:13075#sec2"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:13075#sec2"},{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:13075#sec2-b"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:13075#sec2-b"},{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:13075#sec2-c"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:13075#sec2-c"},{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:13075#sec2-d"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:13075#sec2-d"},{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:13075#sec2-e"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:13075#sec2-e"},{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:13075#sec3"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:13075#sec3"},{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:13075#sec3-b"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:13075#sec3-b"},{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:13075#sec3-c"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:13075#sec3-c"},{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:13075#sec4"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:13075#sec4"},{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:13075#sec4-b"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:13075#sec4-b"},{"aligned_current_scopes":["EO:13075#sec4-c"],"alignment":"exact_quote_and_source","different_current_fields":[],"scope_id":"EO:13075#sec4-c"}],"source_pins":[{"held_text":{"expected_sha256":"9fc04faf535b5640b75997c4fcd743cec3b85e0cbdf52
